text:
The Lightning are playing through the strangest storyline in the league: Nikita Kucherov has told them he won't re-sign and asked for a trade, as the Associated Press reported on Oct. 30. He is still producing, two assists here and six points in two games per CBS Sports. And on a night when Tampa Bay was missing Brayden Point (on injured reserve), Anthony Cirelli and Erik Cernak, the players around him carried a 3-1 win in Columbus.

Brandon Hagel was the best of them. He tipped in the opening goal at 2:57 of the first, set up Jake Guentzel's go-ahead goal 66 seconds into the third, and then beat Jet Greaves with a slap shot at 7:41 on a chance our model gave 6%. Six shots, two goals, an assist and 1.06 expected goals of his own, the quality of chances he generated. Guentzel's goal was the swing of the game, taking Tampa Bay's win chance from 48% to 73%.

Columbus had more of the puck, 72 shot attempts to 54, but less of the danger. At even strength the Lightning built 3.11 expected goals to 2.13, and they owned the second period 1.23 to 0.46 even though nobody scored in it. Guentzel had a 30% look in that period that didn't go in, and Greaves finished about even with expectation. The Blue Jackets' goal came on the power play, Matthew Knies tipping one in at 12:20 of the first. Tampa Bay drew zero power plays all night and didn't need one.

Dennis Hildeby made 28 saves on 29 shots, 1.8 goals better than those shots deserved, and was named the third star. With Andrei Vasilevskiy telling TSN he hopes "that something will change" between Kucherov and the club, a backup winning a road game like this is useful news for Tampa Bay.

Columbus has a bigger worry than the result: Daily Faceoff reported Sean Monahan left the game with an upper-body injury. He had an assist on Knies's goal in 10 minutes before leaving.
headline: Hagel and Guentzel carry a thin Lightning past Columbus
